name: Neyyappam
subtitle: dark ghee-fried rice and jaggery fritters, crisp outside and soft within

ingredients.note: any short or medium grain works

ingredients.qty: 1/2 cup, cut into small thin slivers
ingredients.note: fried in ghee first, then folded through
traditional, and it stops the sweetness cloying
ghee is what makes it neyyappam; oil gives a lesser thing
for lift, added at the last moment

prepNotes: Soak the rice at least 4 hours, or overnight, then drain it thoroughly in a sieve for 15 minutes.
Make the batter and rest it 2-3 hours before frying — unrested batter fries flat and heavy.
You need an appakara or aebleskiver pan for the classic shape; otherwise fry spoonfuls as small round fritters in a deep kadhai.

steps.text: Melt the jaggery with 100ml water over medium heat until dissolved, about 5 minutes, then strain through a sieve and cool to lukewarm.
steps.tip: Cool the syrup before it meets the rice. Hot syrup part-cooks the batter and it will never rise.

steps.text: Grind the drained rice with the cooled jaggery syrup and the remaining 50ml water to a thick, smooth batter — thicker than dosa batter, roughly the consistency of cake batter.
Beat in the crushed cardamom, dry ginger powder and salt, then cover and rest the batter 2-3 hours at room temperature.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan and fry the coconut slivers for 3-4 minutes until golden at the edges, then fry the sesame for 20 seconds.
Fold the fried coconut, sesame and all the ghee from that pan into the rested batter.
Stir in the baking soda if using, right before frying, and do not let the batter sit after this.
Heat the remaining ghee in a kadhai over medium heat until a drop of batter rises to the surface within 3 seconds without browning instantly.
steps.tip: Too hot and the outside darkens while the centre stays raw batter. Medium heat, patiently.

steps.text: Drop in tablespoons of batter, 4-5 at a time, and fry 3 minutes until the undersides are deep mahogany.
Flip each one and fry a further 2-3 minutes until puffed, dark and firm at the edges.
steps.tip: Test one first. If it collapses on flipping, the batter is too thin — beat in a tablespoon of rice flour before continuing.

steps.text: Lift onto a rack to drain and cool, and let the ghee come back to temperature between batches.
Serve at room temperature, when the outside has crisped and the inside stays soft.

storage: Keeps a week in an airtight tin at room temperature and up to 3 weeks refrigerated. No reheating needed — bring back to room temperature before eating.
